panel.summary: Unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25MB bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
panel.evidence: `@SkipThrottle()` (yorkie-event.controller.ts:32) removes the only global rate limit (ThrottlerGuard registered as APP_GUARD in app.module.ts:113, 120 req/60s). The route needs no JWT/API key, so any client that can reach the backend port hits it. Express body-parser runs *before* guards, and main.ts:47-56 applies `limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT` (25MB default) to all JSON routes including this one, and additionally *retains* the raw buffer (`req.rawBody = buf`) only for this path — so each request pins the full 25MB buffer plus the parsed object until the guard rejects it, and the guard then computes an HMAC over those 25MB before rejecting. Attack: send many concurrent `POST /internal/yorkie/events` requests with 25MB JSON bodies and a garbage `X-Signature-256`; every request is fully buffered, doubled in memory, and HMAC'd with no rate limit → memory/CPU exhaustion of the backend. Nothing in the repo restricts the path at an ingress (no manifests present; the same process serves the public API on the same port). Mitigation would be a small per-route body limit (webhook payloads are a few hundred bytes) and/or a generous-but-finite throttle instead of a blanket skip.
